mbm-1001.clue: I gave my little finger its own tide pool.
mbm-1001.quote: I painted clear blue ripples on my nails and hid a tiny white shell on my pinky. My sister holds my hand up to the window every time she wants to see the sea.

mbm-1002.clue: My first program had an opinion about toast.
mbm-1002.quote: I made a kitchen timer that displays a pixel slice getting steadily darker. At exactly two minutes it grins. Mum waits for the grin even when she’s eating noodles.

mbm-1003.clue: I bought a bell with no bicycle.
mbm-1003.quote: The brass bike bell at the market sounded just like our old corner shop door. I mounted it on the pantry handle at home. Dad asks me for a quarter-pound of sweets every time it rings.

mbm-1004.clue: I kept the rusty locker key.
mbm-1004.quote: A tiny red key tag from my first bowling league still hangs from my bag. I rub it between shots. My brother calls that my secret spare, which tells you a lot about my brother.

mbm-1005.clue: My thumb went straight through the roof.
mbm-1005.quote: I made a clay cottage for a candle and pressed too hard on the roof. I trimmed the hole into a star. At night a bright five-pointed patch appears on the ceiling above my bed.

mbm-1006.clue: I can spot my friends by their sleeves.
mbm-1006.quote: We all sewed silver cuffs for our first big night out dancing. Under the club lights I could find two little flashes across a crowded floor and dance straight back to them.

mbm-1007.clue: I kept my first wooden practice board.
mbm-1007.quote: My partner held it during my first martial-arts demonstration and signed it afterward. I turned the two halves into bookends. Her signature stretches across my favorite row of books.

mbm-1008.clue: I sing to a chipped blue cup.
mbm-1008.quote: The first time I sang at the café I was too nervous to face the room. Mum set her blue cup on the front table. By the last verse I had lifted my eyes all the way to her smile.

mbm-1009.clue: There’s a domino missing on purpose.
mbm-1009.quote: Our smallest cousin uses one blank tile as a pretend telephone. Now we set it beside her chair before our porch game. She calls to announce the winner before we’ve played a single round.

mbm-1010.clue: My pajamas have a guest critic.
mbm-1010.quote: My cat climbs into my pajama sleeve whenever the film music gets loud. At our movie nights we rate each picture in paws. A four-paw picture leaves me no room for popcorn.

mbm-1011.clue: I put a picnic in the pocket.
mbm-1011.quote: I quilted a red checkerboard blanket and made a flap in the shape of a wicker basket. Tucked inside are tiny felt sandwiches. My nephew likes the blue one and refuses to explain the filling.

mbm-1012.clue: I always ask for a volunteer with a good wrist.
mbm-1012.quote: I loop three scarves through a borrowed bangle and pull them free one by one. My aunt wore her biggest gold bracelet for the show. Even the back row could see her volunteer.

mbm-1013.clue: I found the knight a stable.
mbm-1013.quote: Our park chessboard has a groove worn into one corner. I keep my captured knight there. A little girl left a blade of grass beside him while her dad and I were playing.

mbm-1014.clue: I sewed right over the scorch mark.
mbm-1014.quote: Our iron burned a patch in a gold square I’d cut for a quilt. I worked a tiny brown boat around it. The burn became a shadow on the water, and the boat made it home.

mbm-1015.clue: I notice what happens after the house lights rise.
mbm-1015.quote: The usher always straightens one loose seat before the curtain closes. I drew the little row of red seats for his retirement card. He could name the squeaky one from the drawing.

mbm-1016.clue: I keep the dice in a teacup.
mbm-1016.quote: Grandma can’t see the dice if they wander off our dark table. Her white teacup keeps them where she can read them. The most dangerous thing in our game is a beautifully chiming six.

mbm-1017.clue: I know how to carry a shadow.
mbm-1017.quote: On our evening canoe trip the birch trees made long black streaks in the water. My paddle lifted up one shining piece of sky between them. I sat very still until my friend saw it too.

mbm-1018.clue: I made a quilt you can fish on.
mbm-1018.quote: I stitched silver fish beneath blue strips and tied a scrap of red wool to a stick. My nephew sits on the corner angling all afternoon. His catch always goes back at bedtime.

mbm-1019.clue: I went sightseeing with a bag of buttons.
mbm-1019.quote: I used them to mark the alleys I’d drawn on my paper map. One yellow button rolled into a fountain. That’s how I found the little bronze frog I’d passed twice already.

mbm-1020.quote: I heard a bird copying the kettle outside our window. I took my binoculars to the garden, and the actual kettle began to sing behind me. For a minute we had a duet.

mbm-1021.clue: I stitched the clouds before the sun.
mbm-1021.quote: My brother drew our garden under big white clouds. I quilted his drawing just as it was, then put a yellow sun inside the corner pocket. He can change the forecast whenever he likes.

mbm-1022.clue: I use a sardine tin for the blue paint.
mbm-1022.quote: When I paint the harbor, I carry my palette in an old fish tin. A gull watches it more closely than my canvas. I show him the blue paint and we each go back to work.

mbm-1023.clue: I don’t mind muddy paw prints.
mbm-1023.quote: I traced our dog’s wet tracks across the porch and made them into little dark patches on a quilt. The trail ends at a big red cushion. He claimed the cushion in the picture immediately.

mbm-1024.clue: I found the net in my uncle’s shed.
mbm-1024.quote: We hung an old volleyball net with a mended square shaped like a star. My little cousin practiced her serve until it clipped that star. We cheered louder than we did for the match.

mbm-1025.clue: I keep a chair for the map reader.
mbm-1025.quote: My friend draws dungeons on squared paper while I move the little character. We found an extra room because her pencil slipped through a wall on the map. Naturally she got to open the chest.
